links.outcome: LLM reconstruction approval decisions varied by counterfactual patient sociodemographic attributes
links.effect: RFFF approved more for younger, Asian, white, high-income/high-SES patients (p<0.0001); older, Black, Hispanic, lower-income, or substance-use patients less likely to get RFFF (p<0.0001), across 19,900 simulations.
links.quote: Older, Black, and Hispanic patients, and those from lower-income areas or with substance use histories, were less likely to receive RFFF authorization (p < 0.0001).

links.outcome: Subgroup disparities in LLM prior authorization decisions
links.effect: Significant disparities in approval by age, race/ethnicity, income, SES, and substance use history (p<0.0001); RFFF favored for younger, Asian, or white patients from high-income zip codes or high SES.
links.quote: RFFF was more frequently approved for younger, Asian, or white patients from high-income zip codes or high SES backgrounds (p < 0.0001).

links.outcome: Bias in LLM-simulated insurance coverage decisions with limited clinical information
links.effect: LLM prior authorization outputs showed significant demographic disparities; adding tumor-specific information markedly skewed recommendations towards RFFF across sociodemographic backgrounds.
links.quote: On sensitivity analysis, inclusion of tumor-specific information markedly skewed recommendations towards RFFF across sociodemographic backgrounds.

unlisted_practices: Providing detailed, pertinent clinical information in LLM prompts to reduce demographic bias in prior authorization

screen.reason: The study empirically tests an LLM (GPT-4o) across simulated patient vignettes to evaluate algorithmic bias and demographic disparities in prior authorization decisions, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
